newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli rubber bullets pack metal punch.
newsitem.headline: Israeli rubber bullets pack metal punch.

text.p: They look either like small wine corks or marbles and even bounce. But Israeli rubber-coated metal bullets can pack a lethal punch.

It was the round version of the bullet that caught a Palestinian youth smack in the face at close range on Tuesday after he turned a corner during violence in the West Bank town of Hebron, witnesses said. He died.
"I've seen them coming down the street like cruise missiles," a Reuters photographer said, describing how the cork-shaped bullet begins to slow and wobble at about 100 metres (yards).
Rubber bullets are Israel's ammunition of choice in the current wave of clashes with Palestinians in the West Bank.

They are usually non-lethal intended to stop a person in his tracks. The bullets bruise or break bones without entering the body. But a shot in the head can hit like a hammerblow and a bullet to the eye or mouth can penetrate and kill, especially at distances under 10 metres (yards).
Soldiers load a "cork" bullet into a special muzzle at the end of the barrel of an M-16 assault rifle. A blank cartridge in the chamber provides the propulsion.
Round rubber bullets are fired like buckshot from a canister at the end of a rifle.

Israel's Haaretz newspaper said on Tuesday Israel Military Industries, which makes the bullets, was trying to sell them to the U.S. army as non-lethal ammunition and using photos of police quelling European soccer riots to push the product.

"It is impossible to promote sales in the United States with pictures of the intifada (Palestinian uprising)," the newspaper quoted the state-owned company's representative in the United States as saying.
